Chapter 70 is the state education aid formula. Lands UNRESTRICTED in the general fund — a school-caused receipt, not school money.
School cost reimbursement — the circuit breaker. See the assumption about whether this duplicates fund 2640.
**Missed in the first pass.** Special education reimbursement.
**Missed in the first pass.** Charter school reimbursement — state aid to the town for resident pupils at charters.
Pre-school tuition.
School building authority. $474,239 a year through FY2022, zero now.
School transportation.
Student bus fees — and see the worked example. Charged, and zero here.
E-Rate is the federal telecoms discount for schools and libraries. Could be either.
Ten characters. Nothing settles it.
Professional development — for whose staff is not stated.
“SD” is School Department or Sewer District, and both exist in this ledger.

**Not buses.** BUSINESS certificates. It sits among marriage licences, certified vitals, street lists, genealogy, dog licences and raffle permits — the Town Clerk’s fee schedule. *An error of mine, caught by reading the column instead of matching a substring.*
**Not transportation.** A TRANSFER. It sits with `OP TRAN AG`, `OP TRAN CP`, `OP TRAN SR`, `OP TRAN TR` — the operating transfers. Same error, same cause.
Transfer, as above.
Transfer, as above.
Bus rental, or business rental. Zero in FY26 either way.
The general fund.
Lost books and technology — charged to students.
Its cash journal says CHAPTER 658 ATHLET and it refunds families by name.

School lunch.

Special education circuit breaker.
Displaced students.
Underground storage tanks — a public works and fire matter, not a school one.
Comprehensive school health services.
Arts and cultural — the district or the Cultural Council. The #718 code is not paired with a program name anywhere here.
“Regional dissemination” #321, FY12. Dormant and undefined here.
A Blue Cross mini grant — school wellness or town employee wellness.
Tech Prep is a federal vocational-education program.
A Tufts University grant; “HEAT” is not expanded anywhere here.

rows.label: ESSER — federal pandemic relief for schools

NOT paired anywhere in our data. Three funds carry a bare 240 and no name. Read as IDEA special education from outside knowledge — **flagged, because these are the two largest grant spends at $229,398 and $179,637**

rows.why: Named `WRRS ASSESSMENT`. The Worcester Regional Retirement System sets it; the town pays it.
Named `STATE ASSESSMENTS` — the Cherry Sheet charges.
Named `MONTY TECH ASSESSMENT`. A regional school district assesses its member towns.
Montachusett Regional Planning Commission — a regional body assessing its members.
Nashoba Associated Boards of Health — a regional district.
Nashoba Nursing — same.
Named `PRINCIPAL SERIAL LOANS`. Repayment of borrowing authorised by votes already taken.
Named `INTEREST SERIAL LOANS`. Same.
Loan administrative fees.

Town Meeting votes the school bottom line; the School Committee allocates within it. Its own minutes carry `Review & Approve Line Item Transfers` as a standing agenda item, with transfers voted line by line.
School non-recurring, a separate article.
A public library is governed by elected trustees.
Health insurance, active and retiree. Rates and shares are set by bargaining and by the insurer, not by a vote on an amount.
Workers compensation — claims driven.
Unemployment compensation — claims driven.
Liability insurance — premium driven.
